title: Achieving your goals through individualism
summary: A philosophical monologue arguing that a strong individual self is the foundation of any healthy collective, and that YouTube fitness fandom is a form of collectivism that strips viewers of identity. He ties individuality to lifting: lifting rewards personal responsibility with direct feedback and builds a strong self, while advising balance so individualism does not become isolation.
claims: Building a strong individualistic drive is the most important thing you can do, both in life and in fitness, because it carries you forward
Self-betterment and fulfilling the needs of body and spirit should always be your number one priority, never replaced by anything
The collective stems from the individual, not the reverse: individuals can exist without the group, though their full potential may need the group
Individuality and collectivity are different from the ideologies of individualism and collectivism; the cliche of ruthless Western individualism is widely overblown
Asian countries often cited as collectivist actually rest on very high personal standards and personal responsibility; good collectivism requires strong individuals first
Evil collectivism (communism) shames people into surrendering individuality for the supposed good of the group, while only a tiny elite on top benefits
YouTube fitness is collectivism run rampant: the YouTuber is the defined individual and the viewers are an anonymous mass whose individuality gets suppressed
A strong cohesive group is built from strong individuals pairing up; a group whose members give up the self is a group of sheep or slaves
Humans are programmed to care about those close to them; people claiming to care about everyone are hypocrites trying to look moral
Morality requires agency: helping a hurt cat by choice is moral, doing it because a law forces you is not; the same split exists between charity and welfare
The more toxic a fitness channel becomes, the more sway the YouTuber gains, until much of the audience obeys whatever he says
Never be reverent toward anyone; respect those you judge deserving, never someone just because others respect them
Being attacked by a group for your opinion is a good sign that you have preserved your individuality, so keep going
You lift purely for personal gain and that is fine; society calls lifting vain because it resents visible self-improvement it gave up on
If a group does nothing for you, leave it; most likely the group needs you more than you need it
The strong seeking the strong creates accountability and awareness; the weak seeking the weak breeds victim mentality, slave morality and comfortable safe spaces
Lifting is personal responsibility: put in the work and you get results; many people who complain of no progress are simply lazy in their training
Someone with a strong sense of self is his own harshest critic and therefore becomes resilient to outside critique
The best lifters are individualistic, sometimes to a fault: at a high level some stop being receptive and think they know everything, which is a problem if they stall
As you learn more you will need his videos less; reaching the point where you know what he will say is a moment of pride
To make a toxic collective crumble, simply leave and do not engage; criticizing it may only feed it
Charisma is individuality; YouTube fandom is a bizarro version of a group where fans feel they belong to a role model who has no contact with them
Never place your own identity in the hands of someone else; be yourself
Rampant individualism is also dangerous: the isolated individual becomes beast-like and may lack help when he needs it; the balance is closer to the individualistic side without going overboard
Lifting is the best immunization against forced collectivism because it gives direct feedback from your own work; strong, big naturals tend to have a strong, big self
Individuality and lifting feed each other: losing the self leads to giving up on training more and more
Lifting, being strong and being big are uncomfortable; choose present discomfort over a permanent lack in the future
